decisions: Famille prédéfinie, noir profond et orange braise pour différencier du premier monde.
Corbeau commun, chauve-souris rare, loup épique, dragon légendaire.
Montée de spectacle et de finition shiny selon la rareté, soin artistique pour toutes.
Quatre références fixes pour tous les propriétaires ; pas une créature aléatoire par utilisateur.
Échantillons non publiés ; shiny peint uniquement, animation à réaliser séparément.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE premium collectible creature illustration, vertical portrait 2:3, full-bleed, ideally 1024x1536, no text or frame.
Collection: NOSFY. Predefined family: LES CIMES ÉTEINTES / THE DARKENED PEAKS, creatures born of soot and ember in black volcanic mountains. This family is visually defined by DEEP BLACK AND ORANGE EMBER, nothing else. Shared material DNA: matte charred velvet, fractured obsidian, dark smoked amber, restrained glowing orange ember fissures. A beautiful, ominous, mysterious dark universe. No moonlit silver landscape.
Art direction: dark poetic fantasy fine art, exquisitely tactile detailed painting, striking creature design and instantly identifiable silhouette. Absolutely not ordinary animal photography. Rich readable near-black forms, shadows separated through subtle black-brown values; at least three quarters of the picture very dark. Orange is concentrated into selective ember light and warm metallic reflections, not a bright overall orange background. The detail quality is extremely high in EVERY rarity; rarity changes spectacle, material finish and scale, not care.
Environment: abyssal black volcanic mountain clefts, jagged basalt spires, ancient soot, occasional dim smoky ember dust, enormous shadow masses. No white fog, no snow, no moon, no silver highlights, no blue, no purple, no green, no rainbow, no starry panorama, no bright sky. Restrained pockets of warm light reveal select details against darkness. Black-on-black remains beautifully legible on a phone.
Composition: singular coherent scene, never a grid, never a four-panel board. Keep every essential tip, face and limb within central 80 percent of canvas width and central 80 percent of height; generous breathing room for an existing external card frame. Full creature clearly visible, believable weight and organic anatomy. Depth through broad dark shapes, avoid busy background.
No typography, names, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, border, rarity moons, graphic symbols, ornamental frame or game UI. No armor, necklaces, collars, jewelry, runes, gore, skulls or humans.
COMMON CARD — QUIET, INTIMATE, MATTE. A small solitary raven-like creature perches inside the shelter of a fractured basalt mountain cleft, entire black bird and long tapered tail visible, occupying about 45 percent of image height. Modest, slightly hunched pose, head turned gently toward us. Highly recognizable triangular beak, soft swept-back little feather crest, two natural feet, one dark lively eye with a tiny deep-orange glint. Fine soot-black overlapping feathers, gorgeous soft matte texture, irregular weathered feather barbs and short fine chest down. A few edges near the cheek carry dull oxidized-copper sheen, but NO glowing veins, fire wings, gemstone body, huge halo or elaborate shiny finish. The common is deliberately restrained and endearing, worth keeping for its face and fine workmanship.
Foreground rough black slate with a single weak ember hidden between rocks provides the only very narrow warm reflected light on the beak, claws and lower chest. Behind: a dark diagonal fissure and nearly invisible jagged volcanic walls. Strong intimate composition, large areas of quiet darkness, creature easy to recognize at small size. A faint floating ash grain or two, no firework storm. Beautifully painted velvet-black detail, delicate warm chiaroscuro. Make this unmistakably the humblest member of a black-and-ember family without making it cheap or generic.

RARE CARD — PRECIOUS BLACK-AMBER SHINY MATERIAL. One exquisite unusual bat glides through a narrow volcanic mountain fissure, head slightly turned toward viewer, immense sculptural scalloped wings lifted in a gentle enclosing arc. Whole bat including BOTH wing tips and both natural hind feet entirely inside the image with generous margins; wings span only about 72 percent of image width. Expressive small face, long delicately pointed ears, smoke-black chest fur, tiny intelligent ember-orange eyes. Beautiful, quietly uncanny, not a cartoon and not a snarling horror bat.
Wings are translucent BLACK SMOKED AMBER: fine anatomically coherent orange-copper veins appear buried deep inside almost-black membranes, tiny resinlike internal inclusions, subtle creases and extraordinary glossy material depth. The finish should look like a coveted shiny collectible: sharply controlled mirror-black facets, narrow liquid-copper reflections and rich deep burnt-orange iridescence where a faint ember beam passes through a limited area. Mostly black wings, not broad glowing orange sails. Orange reflections trace a few fingers and thin membrane edges with extraordinary subtle precision. No silver, no white sparkle. Distinctive luminous amber teardrop marking organically embedded near the base of each wing, repeated with very fine detail. Far surfaces disappear in soft charcoal shadow.
The bat is emerging from a pitch-black split in huge basalt walls. A few faint embers drift in a shaft of dark rust-colored dust well below it, giving scale and depth. The RARE's beauty is in its haunting wing silhouette and seductive black-glass/orange sheen, visibly more precious than matte common, less cosmic than a legendary. Lavish detail in face, fur, wing joints and membrane optics, carefully controlled light.

EPIC CARD — POWER, MOTION, SCULPTURAL BLACK AND EMBER. One magnificent ancient wolf strides along a narrow jagged volcanic ledge above an almost invisible chasm, body in three-quarter profile, head turned slightly toward viewer. Entire wolf including four coherent paws and one long smoky tail inside the image. Wolf occupies about 60 percent of image height, face proud, intelligent and alive, not snarling. Long soot-black fur and powerful shoulders, naturally swept-back pointed ears and warm deep-orange eyes; identifiable wolf anatomy, sophisticated extraordinary silhouette.
Its coarse black mane grows in layered wind-swept locks interleaved with natural obsidian shards, organically continuous with the fur rather than worn armor. Select strands are ember-orange deep within the roots; gusts reveal a narrow luminous current beneath black outer fur. Finely detailed mirrored black-opal facets along shoulder and spine catch intermittent copper-orange SHINY reflections. Fine ash dust trails off the paws. The edge of the neck mane curls in one distinctive crest, like the outline of a dying flame, but it is tangible dark fur not a big fire. All other body areas remain beautifully matte-black to give material contrast. Extreme fine detail in whiskers, damp nose, layered fur, subtly chipped mineral surfaces and the weight of paws on stone.
Black mountain walls rise impossibly tall behind. Only a weak distant ember seam near bottom provides a low warm glow, no bright lava river or exploding volcano. Asymmetric forward-moving composition, commanding presence, orange light reveals selected planes through vast darkness. Much more epic than the intimate raven, physically more powerful than the bat, still less monumental and less ornamentally mineral than the dragon.

LEGENDARY CARD — THE MASTERPIECE, MONUMENTAL AND EXTRAORDINARILY SHINY IN BLACK AND ORANGE. One ancient colossal dragon rests coiled around the jagged broken crown of a black volcanic mountain. Camera looks up from a dark chasm, dragon's elegant long neck and head emerge from the surrounding shadow, one great wing half-unfurled in a tall sculptural arc and the other visibly folded behind the body. Entire dragon including horn tips, wing tip and curling tail contained within the picture with generous margins. ONE anatomically coherent creature: two hind legs, two forelegs, two attached wings, one tail. Long noble narrow face and amber eyes readable near the central upper third. Beautifully frightening ancient intelligence; not cute, not a fairy dragon, not a stock red fantasy dragon and no fire breathing. No mouth full of glowing flames.
Its scales are exquisite layered BLACK OBSIDIAN AND BLACK OPAL: fine overlapping geometric growth, sharp polished edges alternating with matte soot-filled recesses, thick translucent dark-smoked glass on horns and crest. Visually astonishing SHINY finish: liquid copper and burning-amber glints travel along selected scale planes and micro-faceted edges, deep orange iridescence seen inside jet-black crystal, small razor-sharp copper highlights against lustrous black; NO rainbow, silver or white diamond sparkle. Chest plates and crown scales have mineral depth with microscopic inclusions and naturally fractured amber veins. Extreme close-view detail in every revealed scale, age-worn horns, articulated claws, fine wing-membrane ribs and tiny embers buried in black glass. The wing membrane is almost black, shot through with only a FEW incredibly fine deep-orange veins, not a luminous orange sheet.
The neck, wing and tail form a majestic unmistakable silhouette echoing the jagged mountain crown, dragon and mountain seem to have grown from the same primordial material. Black basalt pillars fall into abyssal darkness below. A concealed volcanic ember seam lights a very limited lower area, orange reflections reveal the dragon from within the black, no giant bright lava background. A few scattered glowing ash specks emphasize impossible scale. Cinematic, painterly and sublimely dark. More extraordinary material richness and presence than any other card: an ancient living black jewel that one wants to look at for a long time. Preserve broad calm masses so the lavish microdetail does not turn into visual clutter. Predominantly deep black picture, jewel-like orange tightly controlled.
